transcript.text: I just bought a gym two months ago and
it's been a nightmare. I have a
full-time job that pays well. I just got
sucked in by what looked like a great
deal and the idea of owning a business
on the side. Now it's a complete
disaster. I don't have time to actually
run this thing. What am I going to do
from here?
>> [sighs]
>> This sucks.
The reality is you bought a small
business
and you thought that a small business
would be a passive investment. When the
reality is it couldn't be further from
that. You are learning a very expensive
lesson right now. Either
you will have to lose the money that you
put into the business or you will have
to lose the money that you make from
your job
in the hopes that you'll be able to
learn the business fast enough to turn
it around.
Now I don't know you well enough to know
which of those is lower risk for you.
I would go to a broker and consider
selling it to regain as much as I could
from my original investment unless you
want to go all in on this because it's
going to take all in attention to make
this work especially if it already has
holes in it because you're the only one
who there who's going to give a
about it making money. Everyone else is
probably unfortunately not compensated
enough to care. So you took the risk and
now you got to do the work to make it
work.
